title: Cascade, specificity, and inheritance
summary: Write selectors that win for the right reason and avoid !important.

scenario.briefing: The call-to-action button is blue even though the design system says accent red. A broad selector and an !important rule are fighting. Rewrite the CSS so the button uses the accent color through normal specificity.

objectives.description: Use a selector with appropriate specificity.

hints: Target the button with .card .cta rather than a bare element selector.
Use .card .cta { background-color: #B54131; color: #fff; } and delete the !important rule.

misconceptions.description: Reaching for !important to win a specificity fight.
misconceptions.feedback: !important breaks the cascade and makes future overrides harder. Fix specificity instead.

misconceptions.description: Believing the universal selector beats class selectors.
misconceptions.feedback: The universal selector has zero specificity. Class selectors always beat it.

sections.title: The cascade
sections.body: When multiple rules match, the browser weighs origin, specificity, and source order. Later rules win only when specificity is equal.

sections.title: Specificity
sections.body: Inline styles beat IDs, IDs beat classes, classes beat elements. !important overrides all of them but creates maintenance debt.

vocabulary.definition: The weight the browser assigns to a selector.
The algorithm that resolves conflicting CSS rules.
Passing computed values from parent to child.

steps.title: Fix the cascade
steps.prompt: Edit styles.css. Make .card .cta use the accent background without !important.

files.content:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Store</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <article class="card"><button class="cta">Add to cart</button></article>
</body>
</html>

tests.description: The button uses the accent background.

hints: Delete the blue button rule or raise the accent rule's specificity.
Use .card .cta { background-color: #B54131; color: #fff; } and remove the button rule.

steps.title: Cascade claims
hints: !important is an escape hatch, not a plan.
Select class beats element and tie-breaking; reject universal wins.

statements.label: A class selector beats an element selector.
Source order breaks ties between equal specificity.
The universal selector beats class selectors.

steps.explanation: Specificity and source order resolve conflicts. !important overrides them but creates maintenance problems.
